paragraphs: Friend, think about this one. Joshua is old, and the LORD tells him, "very much of the land remains to be possessed." (Joshua 13:1) Joshua had already helped win the land west of the Jordan, and there was STILL a whole wall of empty cookie boxes left. The big idea is that God's work is bigger than one season of your life, and an unfinished list doesn't mean you did it wrong.

Now look at who does the driving out. The LORD says, "I Myself will drive out before the Israelites." (Joshua 13:6) He also tells Joshua to divide the land by lot, so the people get ready to receive it before every bit of it is taken. I think that's a gift, friend, because the God who promises is the One who finishes, and you get to rest your whole weight on that.

Then the chapter ends on Levi, and this is the part I love. Levi got no land from Moses. Instead, "The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, just as He had promised them." (Joshua 13:33) Every other tribe got a map, and Levi got God Himself. So keep baking, baker, even when the list looks long, because the best thing you can hold is not the land. It's the LORD.
